newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS - UCB denies it planning takeover.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UCB denies it planning takeover.

text.p: Belgian fine chemicals, drugs and plastic films group UCB is sitting on excess cash and looking for a major takeover in one of its core businesses, KB Securities analyst Juergen Fryges said.
The target was "most likely in the speciality chemical or pharmaceutical sector. Predominant regions are the U.S. and Asia," he said in a recent research note.
But UCB spokesman Alain Douxchamps told Reuters, "There is nothing going on. I haven't heard anything. I don't know why (this analyst) is writing that. These are suppositions."

Fryges' bid speculation marks a swing in sentiment from a few months ago when amid almost relentless buying of UCB shares, the company was rumoured to be the target of industry majors such as Solvay and Johnson & Johnson.
Fryges said he raised the share price target for UCB to 144,000 to 146,000 Belgian francs and upheld his 'accumulate' rating. His previous target of 133,100 had been set on June 24.
On a generally firmer Brussels bourse UCB closed up 1,900 francs at 124,400 on Tuesday.
Fryges said recent takeover rumours and the illiquidity of the stock had pushed UCB to a record 153,000.
But a correction meant there was space for a further rally after the expected announcement of the registration of UCB's star anti-allergy drug Zyrtec in Japan.
UCB expects to launch Zyrtec on the Japanese market early in 1998 after getting a registration towards the end of this year.
It plans to launch Zyrtec in Japan together with Sumitomo and an additional partner.
In the U.S. where Zyrtec has been on the market for over 20 months it has been a runaway success. Sales by UCB and its partner Pfizer reached $115 million in the first half.

Pharma is by far the largest contributor to ordinary profits at UCB. First-half pharma profit rose to 2.36 billion francs from 1.93 billion in the same 1996 period. At the group level ordinary profit increased by 33 percent to 3.89 billion francs.
Fryges at KB Securities put the size of the market for anti-allergics in Japan at $500 million, or about a third of the U.S. market.
He said a split of UCB shares by January 1, 1999 would make the stock more attractive for small investors and increase its liquidity. Terms of the split have yet to be announced.
A price of 124,400 for one UCB share equals $3,288. That compares with prices of $35 to $135 for stocks in Wall Street's Dow Jones index.
